answer: In PoA, identity verification uses a Wesolowski VDF: a prescribed chain of continuous, sequential modular squarings followed by a compact proof that can be checked efficiently. A sybil operator may create many clone identities, but every clone requires its own time-dependent chain; GPUs can replicate hardware yet cannot shorten any chain by parallelizing its dependent squarings. Thus admission is constrained by elapsed physical time, whether identities are labeled meadow, onyx, or tundra.
